subject: sr-home-science
title: Model Question Paper 3
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 80 (with one optional module) · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks.
Section B: very short answers 2 marks (30–50 words), short answers 3 marks (50–80 words), long answers 5 marks (80–120 words).
Attempt the questions of either Optional Module A (Housekeeping) or Optional Module B (Creative Hand Embroidery) in all sections.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Name any two examples of general ethics. State any two examples of work ethics.
questions.answer: General ethics: sincerity and honesty (also truthfulness, respect for time). Work ethics: regularity and punctuality, and confidentiality (also loyalty).

questions.q: Match the diseases with the therapeutic diets. A: (1) Diarrhoea (2) Hypertension (3) Constipation (4) Fever. B: (a) Low salt (b) High fibre (c) Low fibre (d) High calorie, high protein.
Match Column I with Column II. I: (1) ICDS (2) Spoon-shaped nails (3) Inability to see in the dark (4) Light-coloured hair. II: (a) Kwashiorkor (b) Night blindness (c) Immunisation (d) Anaemia.
True or False. (a) A peeled apple spoils faster than an apple with intact skin. (b) Blanching kills all enzymes permanently.
questions.answer: (a) True: the skin is a protective cover. (b) False: it stops enzyme action for a time by mild heat.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) All work centres in the kitchen should have adequate ________. (b) To save floor space, cupboards should be replaced with ________ storage.
Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) General Provident Fund (b) Debentures. B: (i) Loan to a company at fixed interest (ii) Compulsory saving for salaried employees (iii) Part ownership of a company.

Give reasons for the following behaviour of adolescents: (i) worry about their looks (ii) peculiar talking and dressing (iii) intense love towards a much older person of the opposite sex (iv) feel parents do not understand them.
questions.answer: (i) Rapid body changes make them feel 'on stage'. (ii) They follow the peer group culture. (iii) It is a 'crush', a typical stage. (iv) Rebellion and the generation gap.

questions.q: Identify the two correct steps to help a mentally retarded child. (i) Teach self-help skills (ii) Enrol them in a regular school (iii) Teach him braille and sign language (iv) Involve him in simple household tasks.
Fill in the blanks. (a) Thread count is the number of ________ and ________ yarns per square inch. (b) Rib weave is made by using ________ yarns with ________ yarns.
questions.answer: (a) Warp and weft. (b) Thin with thick yarns (or single with doubled yarns).

questions.q: Match Column I with Column II. I: (1) Baby garments (2) Teenagers (3) School-going children. II: (a) Variety to mix and match (b) Strong and durable (c) Absorbent cotton.

State True or False. (a) Woollen clothes should be soaked before washing. (b) White clothes should be dried in shade. (c) Optical brightening agents are colourless dyes. (d) Silks should be washed by kneading and squeezing.
questions.answer: (a) False: they felt when soaked. (b) False: whites are dried in the sun. (c) True. (d) True.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name four work ethics expected of a doctor.
questions.answer: A doctor should be regular and punctual, keep patients' information confidential, be polite and sympathetic, and keep learning to update knowledge and skills.

or.q: Mention four work ethics expected of a student.
or.answer: A student should be regular and punctual, do her own work honestly without copying, respect teachers and classmates, and be willing to learn.

questions.q: List the five major food groups.
questions.answer: Cereals and grains, pulses and legumes, milk and meat products, fruits and vegetables, and fats and sugars.

or.answer: It is a special modified diet given to a person with a disease to help recovery. It is a modification of the normal diet in consistency, nutrient content or frequency.

questions.q: What is nutritional status? How can it be assessed?
questions.answer: It is the condition of health influenced by intake and utilisation of nutrients. It is assessed by measuring physical growth, recording dietary intake and recognising deficiency signs.

questions.q: Your mother has bought a large quantity of fresh tender peas. Suggest the correct method to freeze them for future use.
questions.answer: Shell the fresh peas and blanch them in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Cool at once, pack in polythene bags removing air, seal and keep in the freezer.

questions.q: Why is satin weave not as strong as plain or twill weave?
questions.answer: Satin has long floats on the surface, which snag easily and so weaken the fabric.

questions.q: What is the difference between a label and a marking?
questions.answer: A label is a piece of paper, plastic or tag attached to a garment with information. A marking is printed on the surface of fabric or 'thaan' for identification.

questions.q: Give one reason each for the statements. (i) Woollen clothes should not be soaked before washing. (ii) Clothes should not be stored when damp. (iii) Blood stains should be removed with cold water.
questions.answer: (i) Soaking leads to felting of wool. (ii) Moisture causes mildew. (iii) Hot water coagulates blood proteins and fixes the stain.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the physical development in middle childhood (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Children gain about 5–7 cm in height and 2–3 kg in weight each year. (ii) The head becomes smaller in proportion to the body (about 1/6) and permanent teeth number 28. (iii) All bones are formed and strong, and boys have more muscle while girls have more fat.

questions.q: Explain the role of the school in adolescence (three points).
questions.answer: (i) A school that is not harsh and respects students' views makes them enjoy studies. (ii) Warm trained teachers recognise talents and motivate; poor teachers lead to drop-outs. (iii) Teachers can bridge the generation gap.

questions.q: Suggest preventive measures for juvenile delinquency (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Remove poverty through loans and vocational training. (ii) Parents should spend time with children and inculcate good habits and values. (iii) Provide recreational facilities and remand homes for reform and vocational training.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the problems faced by consumers and the solutions to them.
questions.answer: (i) Price variation and overcharging: compare prices, buy from reliable shops and check MRP. (ii) Adulteration and poor quality: buy packed and labelled goods with ISI, AGMARK or FPO marks. (iii) Hoarding and black marketing: refuse to pay more and report. (iv) Defective weights and measures: reject irregular weights and check the scale. (v) Deceptive trade practices and poor guidance: do a market survey and avoid sales tricks. (vi) Keep bills and guarantee cards and report cheating to the authorities.

questions.q: Describe the cognitive characteristics of a child of 11 years.
questions.answer: (i) The child differentiates between fantasy and reality. (ii) The child understands another's point of view (empathy) and is not egocentric. (iii) The child has reversibility, thinking backwards through steps. (iv) The child shows conservation of number, volume and mass. (v) The child classifies objects in many ways and arranges them in order (seriation). (vi) The child understands time and speed, such as which car reaches earlier.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Housekeeping): Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: How will you clean a stained wooden chopping board?
questions.answer: Wash it with mild soap and warm water, scrubbing along the grain. Remove stuck food with the back of a knife and dry it in the open air.

questions.q: Write two points on the importance of arranging things in an orderly manner at home.
questions.answer: Things can be found quickly, saving time and energy. The house looks neat and comfortable and gives a pleasant feeling.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Housekeeping): Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain how to change the washer of a leaking tap (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Turn off the mains and unscrew the hand-wheel. (ii) Remove the headgear using two wrenches and take out the stem with the washer. (iii) Replace the old washer with a new one and fix everything back.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Creative Hand Embroidery): Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Differentiate between warm and cool colours.
questions.answer: Warm colours (red, orange, yellow) feel warm and exciting and reduce size. Cool colours (blue, green, purple) feel peaceful and increase size.

questions.q: Where is chain stitch used?
questions.answer: It is used for heavy outlines, or in rows following the outline as a filling.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Creative Hand Embroidery): Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: List the factors influencing the use of colours with examples (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Age and sex: bright colours for children and young adults. (ii) Occasion and season: cool, soft colours in summer; bright and dark colours in winter. (iii) Type of garment, profession and body structure.
